title: Why Europe cannot let the AI sovereignty ship sail
excerpt: Now is Europe's time to act
content_html:
Discussions about technological sovereignty in Europe can tend towards doomerism. It is easy to see why. A handful of hyper-scalers in the US and China control the foundational infrastructure of the modern world. The reliance on these technologies from companies and governments in Europe grows with each week that passes.

Near-total dependence on foreign-hosted and trained AI models presents a massive national security risk. If there isn’t a sovereign layer to your infrastructure, you don’t have control over the future. What if the plug is pulled or if security is compromised?

These are the nightmare scenarios being discussed in boardrooms and government departments across the continent.

Group CEO, SCC.

And yet, Europe has many reasons to feel optimistic in its pursuit of sovereignty. Perhaps the LLM ship has sailed, but it is what comes next that is truly exciting.

In areas such as quantum computing and robotics – and their application across industries including healthcare and climate science – there is evidence that Europe’s combination of engineering talent and deep customer/market knowledge is laying the foundation for the next wave of society-shaping innovation.

This goes to the heart of what AI sovereignty really means: developing a technology that is both a great product, with no compromise on efficiency and scalability, while also solving the biggest possible problems of today or tomorrow.

A time for action

Now is the time to act. Sovereignty, particularly AI sovereignty, is an absolute priority for European governments and, increasingly, for customers and the public as geopolitical tensions escalate. We are already seeing many examples of companies in Europe building parallel IT infrastructure where they would usually be dependent on hyperscalers. There is also a growing trend towards on-premise cloud and data solutions, in a bid to create sovereign solutions.

So the question is, can we, those of us outside the US and China, build the best products that solve the most pressing problems? The answer is a resounding yes, but we need to ensure that our approach isn’t purely defensive. True sovereignty is about more than having the right level of regulation to protect ourselves against external systems we can’t control. If we want to be sustainable, we need to build alternatives that are at least as good; if we compromise on that, it will fail.

If we take healthcare as an example of sovereignty. It is one of the most sensitive industries when it comes to data, given how personal and confidential medical data is. If your life were dependent on an AI solution that could help define the best personalized or predictive care, and that solution was not sovereign, would you hesitate? Of course not. It is a big problem, but there are companies out there nearing a solution.

A fantastic example of this is the French scale-up ALAN, which is increasingly disrupting the whole medical insurance market thanks to a truly end-to-end designed business process. We need to play to our strengths in these use-case areas where technology has a life-changing impact. In June this year, it announced that it had raised €480m, valuing the company at €5.5bn.

Hindering factors

There are, of course, some factors that might hinder our progress, such as overregulation and the constraints that entrepreneurs face. We cannot ignore the challenge of funding; the US benefits from a $30 trillion pension fund that flows massively into the PE and VC markets. We are far away from that in Europe, and we must find solutions urgently.

There are some positive developments, such as the European Union’s flagship €95.5 billion R&D funding program, Horizon Europe, which supports 200-300 groundbreaking scientific discoveries annually across the EU and the UK. But these initiatives are still relatively small and only represent a step in the right direction.

And Europe’s unique digital market is still not as easy to address as the single US or Chinese market. From my experience on the boards of several European scaleups, many of them find it easier to attack the US market once they’ve gained momentum in their home country than to attack another European country. Ultimately, all of these problems need to be solved.

It is also vital that we choose our battles. We shouldn’t be chasing after American or Chinese LLMs or hyperscalers. We will waste time trying to play catch-up. The reality is that we have a proven track record in use case-driven areas, such as healthcare, and that is where we must focus.

Our approach must be to anticipate where the market is moving. Two areas that are emerging as potentially revolutionary are quantum and robotics. The US is already hedging its bets. President Trump recently signed a bill mandating that the US will have a quantum computer by 2028 and requiring that cyber systems adopt post-quantum crypto-consistent solutions. This is what sovereignty is: it’s not hyperscalers; it’s technology that will significantly impact everyone's lives.

The good news is that in Europe, we have many examples of startups producing world-leading technology in quantum and robotics. Ultimately, the success of sovereignty will depend on our ability to build the best products in Europe to solve our greatest problems. We won’t be sustainable if the ‘sovereign’ alternative isn’t as good as the solutions developed elsewhere. In Europe, we have all the tools to achieve sovereignty. But we must act now.

content_html_zh:
关于欧洲技术主权的讨论可能会走向末日论。 很容易看出原因。 美国和中国的少数超大规模企业控制着现代世界的基础设施。 欧洲公司和政府对这些技术的依赖随着时间的推移而不断增加。

几乎完全依赖外国托管和训练的人工智能模型带来了巨大的国家安全风险。 如果您的基础设施没有主权层，您就无法控制未来。 如果插头被拔掉或者安全性受到损害怎么办？

这些都是非洲大陆董事会和政府部门正在讨论的噩梦场景。

SCC 集团首席执行官。

然而，欧洲有很多理由对其主权追求感到乐观。 也许LLM之船已经扬帆起航，但真正令人兴奋的是接下来的事情。

在量子计算和机器人技术及其在医疗保健和气候科学等行业的应用等领域，有证据表明，欧洲的工程人才与深厚的客户/市场知识的结合正在为下一波社会塑造创新奠定基础。

这触及了人工智能主权真正含义的核心：开发一种既是伟大产品的技术，又不影响效率和可扩展性，同时还能解决当今或未来可能出现的最大问题。

采取行动的时刻到了

现在是采取行动的时候了。 主权，特别是人工智能主权，是欧洲各国政府的绝对优先事项，随着地缘政治紧张局势升级，主权也越来越成为客户和公众的优先事项。 我们已经看到许多欧洲公司构建并行 IT 基础设施的例子，这些基础设施通常依赖于超大规模企业。 为了创建主权解决方案，本地云和数据解决方案的趋势也在不断增长。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

所以问题是，我们这些美国和中国以外的人能否打造出最好的产品来解决最紧迫的问题？ 答案是肯定的，但我们需要确保我们的方法不是纯粹的防御性。 真正的主权不仅仅是拥有适当水平的监管来保护我们自己免受我们无法控制的外部系统的影响。 如果我们想要可持续发展，我们需要建立至少同样好的替代方案；如果我们对此妥协，它就会失败。

如果我们以医疗保健作为主权的例子。 鉴于医疗数据的私密性和机密性，它是数据最敏感的行业之一。 如果您的生活依赖于人工智能解决方案，该解决方案可以帮助定义最佳的个性化或预测性护理，并且该解决方案不是主权的，您会犹豫吗？ 当然不是。 这是一个大问题，但有些公司正在接近解决方案。

法国的 ALAN 就是一个很好的例子，它凭借真正的端到端设计的业务流程，日益颠覆整个医疗保险市场。 我们需要在这些技术改变生活的用例领域发挥我们的优势。 今年 6 月，该公司宣布融资 4.8 亿欧元，公司估值达到 55 亿欧元。

阻碍因素

当然，有一些因素可能会阻碍我们的进步，例如过度监管和企业家面临的限制。 我们不能忽视资金的挑战；美国受益于 30 万亿美元的养老基金，该基金大量流入私募股权和风险投资市场。 欧洲离这个目标还很远，我们必须迫切地找到解决办法。

有一些积极的进展，例如欧盟 955 亿欧元的旗舰研发资助计划 Horizo​​n Europe，该计划每年支持欧盟和英国 200-300 项突破性科学发现。 但这些举措仍然相对较小，仅代表朝着正确方向迈出的一步。

欧洲独特的数字市场仍然不像美国或中国的单一市场那么容易解决。 根据我在几个欧洲扩张公司董事会的经验，他们中的许多人发现，一旦在本国获得了动力，攻击美国市场比攻击另一个欧洲国家更容易。 最终，所有这些问题都需要得到解决。

我们选择我们的战斗也很重要。 我们不应该追逐美国或中国的法学硕士或超大规模的人。 我们会浪费时间去追赶。 现实情况是，我们在用例驱动的领域（例如医疗保健）拥有良好的记录，这是我们必须关注的领域。

我们的方法必须是预测市场的走势。 量子和机器人技术是两个正在兴起的潜在革命领域。 美国已经在两面下注。 特朗普总统最近签署了一项法案，要求美国到 2028 年拥有一台量子计算机，并要求网络系统采用后量子加密一致的解决方案。 这就是主权：它不是超大规模的；而是主权。这项技术将极大地影响每个人的生活。

好消息是，在欧洲，我们有许多初创公司在量子和机器人技术领域生产世界领先技术的例子。 最终，主权的成功将取决于我们在欧洲制造最好的产品来解决我们最严重的问题的能力。 如果“主权”替代方案不如其他地方开发的解决方案，我们就无法可持续发展。 在欧洲，我们拥有实现主权的所有工具。 但我们必须立即行动。
